summary: Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992, 1996) at Minobusan University. He was also attested as director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia in 1996.
Hoong Teik Toh works in Tibetology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Harvard University by 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Hayman Wilson was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas' Hospital Medical School (~1804–1807). He held posts at the East India Company, the Kolkata Mint, and served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1831–1860).

Horace L. Friess was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and Heidelberg University. He taught at Johns Hopkins and at Columbia University, where he became Buttenwieser Professor (1962–1966).
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist who held a post at the University of Münster (attested 1978) and later served at Kiel University (~1995–2011).

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999. He was a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995) and lectured at Vienna (1999).

Hosakote Krishna Sastri was an epigraphist and scholar of Indology and archaeology. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (~1891–1925) and served as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).

Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010), having studied under Ha-u Kim and the traditional teacher Cheonghwa.
Hoseong Kim is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He founded the Nihon Bukkyoshi Kenkyujo and was attested as a professor at Dongguk University in 2011.
Hoshu Mitsuhara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who served as a professor (attested 1982) and later professor emeritus (attested 2004) at Koyasan University.
Hotetsu Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and serves as professor and director at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Houn Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Durham University, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji (1962–1963) under teachers including Chisan Kohō. She served as head priest at Unpuku-ji and later founded and led Shasta Abbey.

Howard Zinn was a historian who studied at New York University (~1949–1951) and Columbia University (~1951–1958). He held academic posts at Spelman College (1956–1963), Harvard (1960–1961), and Boston University (1964–1988).

Hoyo Watanabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1951–1961). He spent his career there as a faculty dean (attested 1984–1985), professor (~1973–2004), and special honorary professor (~2004).
Hozen Seki was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hrachia Adjarian was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at the Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University (1923).

Hrishikesh Rajesh Terdalkar works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied under Arnab Bhattacharya, Pralay Manna, and Sowmya Krishnapur, and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (attested 2023–2024).

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a PhD from Temple University and served as an associate professor at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun was a Buddhist leader who founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as abbot (~1967–1985). He studied under teachers including Zhikai and Yinshun, and later held posts at Chinese Culture University (1980) and Tunghai University (1981).
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Fo Guang University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
